decisions.decision: The canonical evaluation command is vetryn eval; evaluate may be an alias.
decisions.rationale: One stable command keeps documentation, CI, and automation contracts aligned.

decisions.decision: High-confidence scanner precision is at least 95% and supported-pattern recall is at least 80%.
decisions.rationale: Patching the wrong call site is costlier than reporting an ambiguous finding.

decisions.decision: V1 requires versioned JSON and human-readable Markdown; SARIF is deferred.
decisions.rationale: The machine and review contracts are required; another report surface is not.

decisions.decision: V1 uses deterministic scorers, hard gates, and an explicit per-call-site minimum recommendation confidence (0.8 by default); LLM judges are deferred.
decisions.rationale: The first upgrade PR must be reproducible offline and explainable. An optional calibrated semantic-rubric scorer is considered only after V1 field evidence shows deterministic evaluation blocks valuable open-ended call sites.

decisions.decision: V1 resolves at most five candidates by default, configurable downward, after hard compatibility and policy filters; it ranks exact-decimal projected workload cost ascending using pinned representative prompt/completion token weights, context limit descending, then canonical model ID ascending.
decisions.rationale: A bounded, workload-cost-first shortlist controls spend and runtime without assuming that prompt and completion usage are equal.

decisions.decision: Catalog assessment is manual by default, scheduling is explicit opt-in, evaluation inputs bind the evaluator executable identity, unchanged normalized catalog and evaluation inputs skip paid candidate execution only when prior evidence is complete, integrity-valid, and policy-reusable, every successful refresh records immutable freshness evidence, and a failed live refresh cannot be represented as current.
decisions.rationale: Installation must not create surprise recurring spend or silently make recommendations from stale provider state.

decisions.decision: Humans own stable call-site IDs in manifests; scanners emit source fingerprints.
decisions.rationale: Semantic identity cannot be inferred reliably from a moving source location.

decisions.decision: Use repo-native Factory-compatible artifacts without a Factory git submodule.
decisions.rationale: The plan contract should be portable without coupling OSS consumers to orchestration internals.

tasks.title: Accept the imported OSS foundation
tasks.objective: Verify the existing public repository, package skeleton, security workflows, and baseline contracts before V1 work builds on them.
semanticInvariants: The imported baseline remains reproducible from its lockfile.
Security workflows retain least-privilege permissions.
stopConditions: A baseline gate cannot be reproduced.
A required security control would be weakened.

tasks.title: Lock the executable V1 plan
tasks.objective: Commit the reconciled product boundary, task DAG, acceptance ledger, golden scenarios, and agent execution contract.
semanticInvariants: This task does not implement scanner, evaluation, recommendation, or patch behavior.
Progress is derived from canonical state and ledger files.
No task executor can accept its own candidate.

As constrained by docs/adr/0005-authorize-bounded-task-shipping.md, network, stored GitHub authentication, and GitHub writes are limited to initial publication after exact-candidate independent local preflight and explicit maintainer authorization, followed by the Factory commit-push lifecycle; the local preflight never satisfies a canonical review gate, and provider access and unrelated network use remain forbidden.

The temporary bootstrap mode in docs/adr/0006-bootstrap-merge-governance.md may satisfy a declared review role only through an authenticated exact-candidate issue comment whose public association provenance is exactly OWNER, MEMBER, or CONTRIBUTOR and whose actor is authorized for the named role by protected-main CODEOWNERS; CODEOWNERS is authoritative, and merge authorization, CI, Codex settlement, and local agent verification remain separate and never supply task review evidence or canonical promotion.
stopConditions: The product contract and task DAG disagree.
Generated progress differs from canonical state.
Implementation code enters the planning-only change.

Initial GitHub publication occurs before exact-candidate independent local preflight, a canonical review gate is credited with that preflight, or a lifecycle write targets anything outside the authorized V1-00 branch, pull request, merge, or post-merge monitoring flow.

A bootstrap review is accepted without an authenticated current-body issue comment whose exact public association provenance is OWNER, MEMBER, or CONTRIBUTOR, bound to this repository, pull request, task, exact candidate, APPROVED decision, and requested role, with the actor authorized by protected-main CODEOWNERS, or merge authorization, CI, Codex settlement, or local agent verification is represented as task review evidence.

tasks.title: Adopt proportional single-maintainer V1 delivery
tasks.objective: Replace bootstrap-only review mechanics with explicit maintainer-owned delivery permissions while preserving exact command evidence and task-scoped product capabilities.
semanticInvariants: Compiled task capabilities remain exactly the task's reviewed product capability boundary.
Maintainer delivery authority is explicit, Factory-lifecycle-only, and never grants provider access.
Exact candidate and gate bindings, redaction, dependency ordering, and generated progress remain enforced.
stopConditions: A product task capability denial is widened by the compiler or delivery policy.
Provider access, ambient secrets, direct main writes, or automatic product merge are authorized.

tasks.title: Define V1 domain and artifact contracts
tasks.objective: Implement versioned core schemas, deterministic IDs, canonical serialization, and fail-closed validation for every V1 artifact.
semanticInvariants: Core remains pure and has no filesystem, network, provider, GitHub, or AST dependency.
Unknown schema versions and invalid states fail closed.
stopConditions: A schema permits fail-open migration behavior.
Sensitive raw inputs are required in durable reports.

tasks.title: Activate the golden-scenario execution skill
tasks.objective: Create the narrowly scoped reusable workflow required to construct and validate the offline V1-02 golden repository.
semanticInvariants: The skill authorizes neither provider calls nor task acceptance or merge.
The skill keeps golden-scenario inputs offline, sanitized, deterministic, and semantically asserted.
stopConditions: The skill authorizes a live provider, credentials, task acceptance, or merge.
The skill duplicates product behavior or adds files outside its narrow process scope.

tasks.title: Authorize one V1-02 review-correction attempt
tasks.objective: Record a narrowly bounded maintainer reauthorization for one fresh V1-02 candidate that addresses five exact review findings without letting V1-02 alter its own delivery boundary.
semanticInvariants: The reauthorization is limited to exactly one additional V1-02 attempt: its canonical state records two consumed attempts, revision 1, and maxAttempts 3.
The only authorized application replay correction is r3754744063: replay the real application call through a deterministic OpenAI-compatible transport.
The only authorized unknown-outcome correction is r3754744064: reject unknown mock outcomes rather than reporting success.
The only authorized stale-source correction is r3754744067: bind refusal to the checked-in source and manifest fingerprint.
The only authorized budget correction is r3754790013: propagate provider budget exhaustion through the SDK-compatible transport.
The only authorized typecheck correction is r3754790019: run golden-fixture typechecking through the repository quality gate.
The process task does not implement product behavior, broaden V1-02 capabilities, or weaken offline, redaction, or fail-closed requirements.
V1-02 cannot begin its reauthorized attempt until this task is accepted with candidate-bound command evidence.
stopConditions: The reauthorization expands beyond one V1-02 attempt or beyond the five recorded review findings.
A product source, package, fixture, workflow, capability, or safety requirement is changed by this process task.

tasks.title: Authorize the V1-02 redaction correction and separate promotion
tasks.objective: Authorize the two post-review V1-02 corrections without adding a fourth attempt, product capability, or unrelated fixture behavior.
semanticInvariants: The reauthorization amends only the still-unaccepted third V1-02 attempt; it does not add a fourth attempt or broaden capabilities.
The only authorized acceptance-separation correction is r3755066013: keep V1-02 pending until a maintainer promotes its exact candidate separately from the executor.
The only authorized redaction correction is r3755066020: recursively scan every durable fixture and expected artifact for credential and protected-output markers.
The process task does not implement product behavior, expand fixture scope, or weaken offline, redaction, or fail-closed requirements.
V1-02 cannot submit this corrective candidate for verification until this task is accepted with candidate-bound command evidence.
stopConditions: The reauthorization adds a fourth V1-02 attempt, product capability, live provider access, or any finding beyond the two recorded review IDs.
A product source, package, fixture, workflow, capability, or safety requirement is changed by this process task.

tasks.title: Authorize the bounded V1-03 accessor and gate correction
tasks.objective: Authorize exactly two post-review V1-03 corrections without self-expanding scanner scope, changing another task's review boundary, or adding an attempt.
semanticInvariants: The authorization is limited to the still-unaccepted V1-03 correction; it retains V1-03 attempt 3 and maxAttempts 3, and never creates a fourth attempt.
The only authorized accessor correction is r3758194562: a later statically named model accessor makes the earlier literal model field ambiguous and therefore not patchable.

The only authorized criterion correction is r3758194569: after preserving the reviewed V1-01 and V1-02 privacy gates, bind V1-03 SCAN-004 to QG-SCANNER-CORPUS, the deterministic gate that exercises its adversarial assertion.
The process task does not implement product behavior, broaden V1-03 capabilities, rewrite another task's acceptance criteria, or weaken privacy, abstention, or fail-closed requirements.
V1-03 cannot begin or submit this corrective candidate until this task is accepted with candidate-bound command evidence.
stopConditions: The authorization adds a fourth V1-03 attempt, product capability, live provider access, or any finding beyond r3758194562 and r3758194569.
A product source, package, fixture, workflow, capability, or safety requirement is changed by this process task.

tasks.title: Activate local adversarial review for high-risk work
tasks.objective: Require a frozen-candidate Factory code review before promotion and push for high-risk V1 tasks, activate the bounded Vetryn trust-review skill before V1-06, and preserve remote Codex as a separate residual gate.
semanticInvariants: High-risk packets place code-review after validation-gate and before commit-push, require candidate-bound review_report lifecycle evidence, and invalidate that evidence when product or contract-bearing candidate bytes change.

Local structured review runs on the frozen candidate before maintainer promotion and the first push; deterministic command gates remain required and remote Codex remains a separate latest-head residual review gate.
The trust-review skill is limited to evaluation, recommendation, and patch trust semantics; it cannot implement, repair, accept, promote, merge, or substitute LLM judgment for deterministic evidence.
Single-maintainer delivery remains in force: this process task does not restore CODEOWNERS, named human-review blockers, or automatic merge.
The task changes process contracts only and does not alter product behavior, provider access, credentials, GitHub authority, or acceptance semantics for completed tasks.
stopConditions: A high-risk packet can reach promotion or push without candidate-bound local review evidence.
Local review replaces deterministic gates or remote latest-head Codex review.
The trust-review skill gains implementation, acceptance, promotion, merge, provider, credential, or GitHub-write authority.
A product source, package, fixture, CI or GitHub workflow, capability, or completed-task acceptance record changes; the authorized WORKFLOW.md operating-contract edit is excluded.

tasks.title: Complete the executable V1-05 packet
tasks.objective: Make the V1-05 packet executable in clean frozen installs and Factory's frozen-candidate review preflight by authorizing only the required workspace, release, and lifecycle-reference contract changes.
semanticInvariants: The correction authorizes only root files mechanically required to add and publish the V1-05 workspace package: .changeset/**, knip.json, package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, and vitest.config.ts.
A publishable-package task declares required release metadata, a minor Changeset marker, and package/example documentation sync in its compiled packet.
Every lifecycle evidence name has one immutable candidate-specific repo-relative ref beneath the trusted Factory artifact namespace, and high-risk V1-05 names its review_report ref explicitly.

The stored-packet lifecycle validator rejects an unbound candidate, authenticates packet identity and every policy-bearing field against current product-contract, plan, lockfile, canonical task, and canonical candidate inputs, including acceptance items, scanner and CI gates, release/documentation intent, and source metadata, and compares JSON objects without key-order sensitivity while preserving array order; only packet revision, lifecycle state label, and ledger/state status-evidence promotion tails may differ while the candidate remains identical.
Publishable-package documentation refs derive from the task's package deliverables and authorized example paths rather than from one provider-specific hard-coded list.
V1-05 retains its existing product acceptance criteria, provider capability, high-risk review gates, retry limit, deterministic ranking policy, and fail-closed semantics.
The process task changes no product source, fixture, dependency version, workflow, credential, provider call, or completed-task acceptance record.
stopConditions: The correction authorizes a root path beyond .changeset/**, knip.json, package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, or vitest.config.ts for V1-05.
The correction changes V1-05 product behavior, acceptance criteria, capabilities, high-risk gates, attempt limit, or provider policy.
A lifecycle artifact ref escapes product/plans/oss-v1/evidence/lifecycle/TASK-ID or does not correspond one-to-one with lifecycle_evidence_required.
A product source, package, fixture, dependency version, CI or GitHub workflow, credential, or completed-task acceptance record changes.

tasks.title: Build the deterministic golden repository
tasks.objective: Create the TypeScript/OpenRouter fixture, reviewed cases, pinned catalog, mock provider, expected artifacts, and offline scenario harness.
semanticInvariants: The golden suite runs without network access.
Fixture secrets and protected output markers never appear in logs or reports.

This reauthorized attempt is limited to r3754744063 application replay, r3754744064 unknown-outcome rejection, r3754744067 stale-source binding, r3754790013 transport budget propagation, and r3754790019 golden-fixture typechecking.
The M0-04 amendment is limited to r3755066013 separate maintainer promotion and r3755066020 recursive durable-artifact redaction scanning.
stopConditions: A scenario depends on live provider state.
Expected snapshots replace semantic assertions.
A proposed change cannot be traced to one of the five M0-03 authorization findings or the two M0-04 authorization findings.

tasks.title: Implement high-confidence TypeScript discovery
tasks.objective: Add the staged TypeScript package, scan supported OpenAI-compatible calls, emit fingerprints and ambiguity, and meet the corpus thresholds.
semanticInvariants: Scanner output never invents the stable semantic call-site ID.
Ambiguous or dynamic calls are findings, never patch targets.
Root workspace support and release metadata are limited to the staged scanner package, its tests, and the previously accepted manifest-init public APIs.

The still-unmerged final scanner-correction attempt is limited to the previously completed abstention remedies, the two current-head precision remedies, and the direct-eval and var-binding safety remedies: erased declarations do not shadow intrinsic direct eval, and a var declaration initializer or loop binding that merges with a verified receiver invalidates that receiver.
The M0-05 authorization is limited to r3758194562 accessor abstention and r3758194569 binding SCAN-004 to QG-SCANNER-CORPUS; it does not broaden discovery or permit source patching.
stopConditions: High-confidence precision falls below 95%.
Supported-pattern recall falls below 80%.
An ambiguous source can be patched.

tasks.title: Implement manifest initialization and validation
tasks.objective: Turn reviewed discoveries into human-owned call-site manifests while preserving stable identity and explicit ownership.
semanticInvariants: Re-scans do not silently rename human-owned call-site IDs.
Each manifest pins a human-reviewed representative prompt/completion token-weight profile with provenance for candidate cost ranking.
Manifest initialization is reviewable and idempotent.
The only root test and typecheck support changes are the explicit paths needed to exercise the new internal core dependency and keep plan fixtures isolated from V1-04 lifecycle state.
stopConditions: An existing stable ID can be overwritten without review.
Invalid manifests are partially accepted.

tasks.title: Implement reproducible OpenRouter catalog snapshots
tasks.objective: Add the staged OpenRouter package, normalize candidate capabilities and pricing, cache immutable snapshots, and replay them offline.
semanticInvariants: Every evaluation cites an immutable catalog snapshot.
Missing or ambiguous pricing and capability data excludes the candidate.
Candidate selection is bounded by repository policy and reproducible from normalized catalog data.
Projected workload cost uses exact-decimal catalog prices weighted by the manifest's pinned representative prompt/completion token profile.
Candidate ranking uses projected workload cost ascending, context limit descending, and canonical model ID ascending.
Every successful live refresh records immutable freshness evidence even when its content-addressed snapshot is reused.
A failed live refresh cannot silently relabel an older snapshot as current.

Workspace and release metadata changes are limited to the staged OpenRouter package, its CLI integration, deterministic test resolution, dead-code analysis, frozen lockfile importer, and required Changeset.
stopConditions: A run can silently use a mutable live catalog.
Unknown pricing is treated as zero.
A missing, invalid, unreviewed, or unprovenanced representative usage profile produces a shortlist.
Candidate selection exceeds its configured bound or changes under identical inputs.
Candidate ranking uses a different field, direction, or tie-break order than the locked ranking tuple.
An unchanged normalized catalog creates a distinct snapshot, omits its new refresh observation, or a failed refresh is reported as fresh.
The lockfile or workspace analysis changes include anything beyond the new OpenRouter workspace importer, internal workspace links, and its existing pinned toolchain.

tasks.title: Implement bounded deterministic evaluation
tasks.objective: Run representative cases against compatible candidates with deterministic scorers, retries, budgets, hard limits, and reproducible artifacts.
semanticInvariants: Hard limits cannot be outweighed by aggregate quality or savings.
Partial, exhausted, or privacy-unsafe runs cannot recommend.
stopConditions: Retries or spend are unbounded.
Raw sensitive input or output enters durable artifacts.
Incomplete evidence can pass.

tasks.title: Implement recommendation policy and reports
tasks.objective: Compare current and candidate runs, enforce non-inferiority and confidence, and emit evidence-backed JSON and Markdown recommendations or abstentions.
semanticInvariants: Savings never compensate for failed quality or hard gates.
JSON and Markdown are derived from the same canonical recommendation.
stopConditions: A recommendation lacks reproducible evidence.
An abstention path produces a patch.

tasks.title: Implement safe source patching
tasks.objective: Generate the smallest reviewable model-pin change only when discovery, identity, source fingerprint, and recommendation preconditions still hold.
semanticInvariants: Stale or ambiguous source never changes.
Only the reviewed model pin changes unless a broader migration is explicitly unsupported.
stopConditions: The source fingerprint is stale.
The patch touches unrelated syntax.
No accepted recommendation exists.

tasks.title: Ship the composite GitHub Action and PR contract
tasks.objective: Package scan, eval, recommend, report, and patch as a least-privilege composite Action with deterministic artifacts and idempotent PR behavior.
semanticInvariants: The Action requests only the permissions needed for the selected mode.
Unchanged inputs do not create duplicate PRs or mutable evidence.
Provider-backed assessment is manual by default and scheduled execution requires explicit repository opt-in.
The evaluation-input digest binds the evaluator tool version and build or commit revision.
An unchanged catalog and evaluation-input digest skips paid candidate execution only when prior evidence is complete, integrity-valid, and reusable under current policy.
stopConditions: Workflow permissions are broader than required.
A failed or abstained run can open a migration PR.
Action reruns duplicate output.
Installation alone enables recurring provider spend.
An evaluator tool version or build/commit revision change reuses evidence produced by older executable code.
Complete reusable evidence is ignored and unchanged inputs trigger provider execution.
Failed, partial, exhausted, privacy-unsafe, or otherwise non-reusable evidence suppresses a later bounded retry.

tasks.title: Validate the beachhead in real repositories
tasks.objective: Prove that qualified recommendation PRs are trusted, merged, safe, and economically meaningful, and assess whether deterministic evaluation blocks valuable open-ended call sites before expanding scope.
semanticInvariants: Recommendation and rollout metrics count only qualified, evidence-backed recommendations.
The field assessment separately records positive blocked-call-site evidence, representative no-findings, or insufficient coverage.

Representative no-findings requires a predeclared eligibility census and direct assessment of at least ten eligible open-ended call sites across at least three FIELD-001 companies, with coverage and exclusions independently reviewed.
Blocked open-ended call sites are never counted as qualified recommendations, and neither no-findings nor insufficient coverage can authorize semantic-scorer expansion.
Customer data and outcomes are recorded without raw prompts or outputs.
stopConditions: A serious quality, safety, privacy, or operational regression occurs.
Savings cannot be attributed to the recommendation.
Customer consent or data handling is unclear.
A semantic-scorer expansion claim lacks sanitized evidence of valuable open-ended call sites blocked specifically by deterministic evaluation.
